outcomeNote: a mishna stating law, with no dispute and no dialectical exchange

segments.he: מַתְנִי׳ בָּאוֹנֵס וּבַמְפַתֶּה לְהָקֵל וּלְהַחֲמִיר, כֵּיצַד? אֶחָד שֶׁאָנַס וּפִיתָּה אֶת גְּדוֹלָה שֶׁבַּכְּהוּנָּה וְאֶת הַקְּטַנָּה שֶׁבְּיִשְׂרָאֵל — נוֹתֵן חֲמִשִּׁים סְלָעִים, וְהַבּוֹשֶׁת וְהַפְּגָם — הַכֹּל לְפִי הַמְבַיֵּישׁ וְהַמִּתְבַּיֵּישׁ.
segments.en: «MISHNA:» There are halakhot «with regard to a rapist and with regard to a seducer that are lenient and» others «that are stringent; how so? Both» one «who raped or seduced» a young woman «who is» the most «prominent in the priesthood and» one who raped or seduced a young woman who is «the lowliest among the Israelites gives» the payment of «fifty sela,» the fine stated in the Torah (see Deuteronomy 22:29). «And» the payments for «humiliation and» for «degradation» resulting from being raped or seduced are assessed differentially; it is «all based on the one who humiliates and the one who is humiliated.»

moves.summary: the mishna spells out the leniency and stringency listed at the head of the chapter for a rapist and a seducer
